intelligence.essence: Shawn's November 17 Hub corrections say one thing from ten angles: the page he sees is for a human — no machine text on it, no gray words, no flat shapes — while the machine's own language rides quietly on the back of every note, where it helps without ever being seen.
intelligence.human_view: The pages you look at get cleaner and more real: the technical chatter under the feed is gone, every word is bright white and readable, and every button and icon feels like a real object you could pick up — while all the machine bookkeeping happens behind the scenes, where it belongs.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine a toy shop window with the price tags and cardboard boxes shoved in front of the toys. We learned to clear the window: toys in front, boxes in the back room. And the toys are real and round, not flat pictures taped to the glass.
intelligence.grandma_view: We used to leave our working notes right on the page he reads — counts, timings, system names. He asked us to take them off, make every word plain bright white, and make every shape feel solid and real. The machinery still runs; it just stays in the back, the way a good kitchen stays out of the dining room.
intelligence.ai_view: Operating rules distilled from SN-3175..SN-3184: (1) no machine text on human surfaces — counts, backend names, check times are removed whole; the greeting stands clean. (2) Text on obsidian is white or layered white (25/19/17); gray text is a defect a checker greps for and names. (3) Every icon/board/button is a ball — round, raised, deep — never a flat circle or an empty ring. (4) Clarity is judged at zoom: icon and circle crisp, separate, real space between. (5) Glow over a face is removed; glow around and shine through stay; 3D elevation outranks glow. (6) Machine/SEO language rides the back of every note; human language rides the front. (7) A link opens the view it names, not the front door. (8) Work consolidates into one round — never re-sent, never split, never shown twice. (9) The menu control sits on the right of the top bar.
intelligence.what_it_means: The front of the system is an experience and the back is an engine, and confusing the two is the defect: every correction in this group moves something from the face to the back, or raises something on the face from flat picture to real object.
whats_inside: The feed, cleaned: machine text removed whole, the greeting standing clean (SN-3175)
The menu control moves right — sidebar or messenger (SN-3176)
No gray text, emphatic again — white or layered white only, checker-enforced (SN-3177)
The ball, not a circle — raised, deep, real; the empty ring fails too (SN-3178)
Depth over decoration: clarity at zoom, glow around not over, 3D not 2D, machine on the back, links that land, one round (SN-3179–SN-3184)

page.machine: 1) Human surfaces carry zero machine text. 2) Text = white/layered-white only; gray is a named defect. 3) Objects: ball form, elevation over glow, glow around/through never over. 4) Zoom test: icon+circle crisp and separate at any size. 5) Notes: machine language on the back, human on the front. 6) Deep links open the named view. 7) One consolidated round per fix.
page.why_it_matters: These ten notes are Shawn designing by correction in real time — each one a thing his eye caught on the live Hub. Together they define the surface contract every interface lane builds against: human in front, machine behind, everything real enough to touch.
page.how_it_connects: Batch 14 distills the next hundred uncovered notes in backlog order (SN-3175 onward) — the 2026-11-17/18 design-and-law dictation wave the Intelligence Loop filed on 2026-11-18. This essence carries the wave's opening movement, the Hub surface corrections; its siblings carry the icon standard (SN-4738), objectnality (SN-4739), the page-to-ten drive (SN-4740), and the operating laws (SN-4741).
page.what_is_in_it_for_you: What you see gets simpler and more solid at once: no clutter, no dim words, nothing flat — and the system still does all its bookkeeping, just where you never have to look at it.
page.the_learning: From now on, a surface is checked as a stranger's eye meets it — grep for gray, zoom the icon, read the page cold — instead of trusting that the machinery underneath being right makes the face right.
